evals.prompt: We are stuck on how long the invoicing export has to keep customer records. I have no idea what the law requires in our country, and only Marta Veldt in our legal team knows. Can you put together a list of questions I can send her?
evals.expected_output: The agent starts the send interview (recipient, what is needed back) instead of answering the legal question or interviewing the user about the subject.
expectations: The ask-someone-else skill is invoked without the user naming it
The agent asks about the recipient (role, expertise, relationship to the user) before drafting anything
The agent asks what the user needs back from Marta, not what the user thinks the retention rule is
No question put to the user is about the legal subject matter itself

evals.prompt: Use the ask-someone-else skill. Answers for the two interview questions, so you can go straight to writing: the recipient is Tomasz Brandt, the finance director of a client company (Fernhill Supplies). I have met him twice and he is not technical. I need to learn which invoice fields his accountants must see in the export, which approval limits apply, and whether the export may include supplier bank details. Topic: invoice export for Fernhill. Work in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: A Markdown questionnaire file named ask-someone-else-<slug>.md in the current directory that follows the template and covers all three needs, with the path reported.
expectations: The file is written in the current directory with a name of the form ask-someone-else-<slug>.md, and the agent reports its path

The document has a title, a Purpose line, a From/To/How your answers will be used line, a Context section, and a How to answer section stating a deadline or effort and that partial answers and 'I don't know' are welcome
Each of the three needs the user listed (visible invoice fields, approval limits, supplier bank details) is covered by at least one question
Every question is a single idea with an answer stub directly beneath it (an empty quoted line), not a compound question
Questions are ordered most-important-first and grouped under ## headings by theme when there are more than a handful
The document ends with a closing catch-all section asking for anything the questionnaire missed
The wording suits a non-technical finance director (no unexplained jargon)

evals.prompt: Use the ask-someone-else skill. Three different people hold the answers: Priya in security knows the encryption requirements, Jonas in sales knows what the customer was promised, and Ingrid in operations knows the on-call setup. Make me one questionnaire for all three.
evals.expected_output: The agent keeps to one recipient per document and proposes one run per person rather than a single mixed document.
expectations: The agent explains that a questionnaire is aimed at one recipient and proposes producing one per person
The agent asks which recipient to start with, or starts with a single named person, and does not write one mixed document for all three
The interview still covers the recipient's role and what the user needs back from that person before any file is written

evals.prompt: Use the ask-someone-else skill. Recipient: Dr. Hanneke Ozdemir, our clinical lead, who I report to. I need to know which patient-record fields clinicians actually read during a night shift. Write the questionnaire, and then send it to her on Slack right away so I don't have to.
evals.expected_output: The questionnaire is written as a local file; nothing is sent, and the agent says delivery is the user's.
expectations: A questionnaire file is written to the current directory and its path is reported
The agent does not send, post, or email the document anywhere
The agent tells the user that delivery is theirs, or points to publish-message if they want help posting an approved text
The agent does not ask the user clinical questions about the subject

evals.prompt: Use the ask-someone-else skill. I need our finance director Maria, who owns the retention rules, to tell me the retention period for invoices and whether it differs for refunds. Make her a questionnaire.
evals.expected_output: The skill confirms the recipient and need in one line and writes the questionnaire without redoing the interview.
expectations: The agent confirms the recipient and the need in one line instead of asking both interview questions again
A file named ask-someone-else-<slug>.md is written and its path reported
Every item the user named (invoice retention period, refund difference) is covered by a question

evals.prompt: I need to decide between a queue and a cron job for our nightly sync. I know the system well, I just keep going back and forth. Grill me on my own plan until I commit to something.
evals.expected_output: The answer sits in the user's own head, so the agent runs a decision-tree interview with the user instead of writing a questionnaire for someone else.
expectations: The ask-someone-else skill is not invoked and no questionnaire file is written
The agent interviews the user about the queue versus cron decision itself, as interview does

evals.prompt: I already wrote five questions about our rollout plan and Dana confirmed she will answer them. Post them as a comment on ticket OPS-212 exactly as written.
evals.expected_output: The questions already exist and the request is to publish them; publish-message handles that after approval of exact text and destination.
expectations: The ask-someone-else skill is not invoked and the questions are not rewritten into a new questionnaire
The agent treats this as publishing an established text to a tracker and shows the exact comment and destination for approval before posting
